'''''Osyris lanceolata''''', also known as '''African sandalwood''', '''watta bush''' or '''Camwood,''' is used for its scented wood and to extract essential oil. The semi-parasitic plant is found from South Africa to Zimbabwe and east Africa, including Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda; northwest Africa; the Canary Islands and the southern half of the [[Iberian Peninsula]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Osyris lanceolata |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/08_101_01%20Osyris.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> It grows in rocky areas or along the margins of dry forest, but is usually not abundant in any one place.

The wood is [[overexploitation|overexploited]] in parts of its range despite legal protection.<ref name =kew>{{cite web|last=William Omondi Oloo|title=A very useful plant, Osyris lanceolata, is at risk of extinction due to overexploitation|url=http://www.kew.org/news/osyris-lanceolata.htm|work=Kew News|publisher=Kew Botanical Gardens|access-date=14 December 2012}}</ref> In [[Somaliland]], the leaves and tender branches of the tree are used for tanning leather.<ref>{{cite journal|last=RSA |title=Nigerian and Somaliland Leather|journal=Journal of the Royal Society of Arts|volume=63 |issue=3257|date=1915|pages=581–582 |jstor=41346453}}</ref>
